0.note: The superscription to this psalm identifies it as a **maskil**. Since the meaning of this word is not certain, you may wish to represent it in its Hebrew form and spell it the way it sounds in your language. See the discussion of that term in the Introduction to Psalms.

1.q: חַֽסְדֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה עוֹלָ֣ם אָשִׁ֑ירָה לְ⁠דֹ֥ר וָ⁠דֹ֓ר ׀ אוֹדִ֖יעַ אֱמוּנָתְ⁠ךָ֣ בְּ⁠פִֽ⁠י
1.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in the Psalms, and follow that approach here and throughout this psalm. Alternate translation: [I will always sing about the covenant faithfulness of Yahweh; indeed, I will tell every generation how faithful you are]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how Yahweh faithfully keeps his covenant]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how faithful you are]
Here, **with my mouth** represents speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by my words]

2.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because I said]

Here Ethan is speaking as if covenant faithfulness were a structure that could be **built up**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Covenant faithfulness will be established] or [You will show covenant faithfulness]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The way you faithfully love]

The expression **will be built up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [you will build up]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how faithful you are]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the heavens after the information about establishing faithfulness. Alternate translation: [you establish your faithfulness in the heavens]

3.q: כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית לִ⁠בְחִירִ֑⁠י נִ֝שְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי לְ⁠דָוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽ⁠י
3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [God said that he has cut a covenant with his chosen; he has sworn to David his servant]

3.q: כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית לִ⁠בְחִירִ֑⁠י נִ֝שְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי לְ⁠דָוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽ⁠י
3.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [I swore an oath to David, my chosen servant]

4.q: עַד־ע֭וֹלָם אָכִ֣ין זַרְעֶ֑⁠ךָ וּ⁠בָנִ֨יתִי לְ⁠דֹר־וָ⁠ד֖וֹר כִּסְאֲ⁠ךָ֣ סֶֽלָה
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [I swore that I will establish his seed until forever, and I will build up his throne to generation and generation]

Here Ethan is speaking as if descendants were **seed** that is planted. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will establish your descendants] or [I will establish your offspring]

Ethan is using **build up your throne** as a common expression of the culture to mean “firmly establish your rule.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will firmly establish your rule] or [I will make your kingdom strong]

Here, **your throne** represents royal authority and rule. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your royal authority]

5.note: Ethan is speaking of **the heavens** as if they were a living thing that could praise God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the beings in heaven praise your wonder]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how faithful you are]

Ethan is using this possessive form to describe an assembly that is made up of the holy ones. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the assembly where the holy ones gather]

6.q: כִּ֤י מִ֣י בַ֭⁠שַּׁחַק יַעֲרֹ֣ךְ לַ⁠יהוָ֑ה יִדְמֶ֥ה לַ֝⁠יהוָ֗ה בִּ⁠בְנֵ֥י אֵלִים
6.note: Ethan is using the question form to emphasize that no one is comparable to Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For no one in the sky arrays with Yahweh; no one compares to Yahweh among the sons of God.]

Here Ethan is speaking as if the heavenly beings were literal **sons of God** who were born from him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [among the heavenly beings] or [among the divine beings]

7.note: The expression **greatly dreaded** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the holy ones. Alternate translation: [the holy ones greatly dread God]

Ethan is using this possessive form to describe a council that is made up of the holy ones. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [council where the holy ones gather]

8.note: Ethan is using the question form to emphasize that no one is like Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [no one is like you, mighty Yah!]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And you are characterized by how faithful you are]
**Yah** is a shortened form of the name “Yahweh,” the God of Israel. You could use the full name if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh]

9.note: Here Ethan is speaking as if the **surging of the sea** represented chaotic forces that oppose God. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You are ruling over the raging of the sea] or [You control the powerful forces of the sea]

Ethan is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it is Yahweh alone who has the power to calm the waves. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you alone still them]

10.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a slain one** is completely defeated and left powerless, so is **Rahab**, the sea monster, after God shattered it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [You completely defeated Rahab, shattering it as one would kill an enemy]

Ethan is stating the pronoun **You** separately, even though the verb already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it was Yahweh himself who accomplished this mighty act. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [You yourself shattered]

Here, **the arm of your strength** represents God’s great power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your mighty power]
Ethan is using this possessive form to describe an arm that is characterized by strength. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [your strong arm]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with your strong arm]

11.note: Ethan is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [also to you belongs the earth]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fullness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [everything that fills it]

Ethan is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that God himself is the one who established the world. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you yourself founded them]

11.q: לְ⁠ךָ֣ שָׁ֭מַיִם אַף־לְ⁠ךָ֥ אָ֑רֶץ תֵּבֵ֥ל וּ֝⁠מְלֹאָ֗⁠הּ אַתָּ֥ה יְסַדְתָּֽ⁠ם
11.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [You created and you own the entire world and everything in it]

12.note: Ethan is referring to all of creation by naming two extremes, **the north** and **the south**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Everything in every direction]

Ethan is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that God alone is the creator. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you yourself created them]

Ethan is speaking of **Tabor and Hermon** as if they were living things that could shout joyfully. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people at Tabor and Hermon shout joyfully because of you]
Ethan is using the term **name** to represent who the person is or to refer to the person’s reputation. Alternate translation: [because of who you are]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **might**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an arm that is mighty]

Here, **hand** represents the power or control of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your power is strong; your authority is supreme]

Here Ethan is speaking as if God’s power were **high** or physically elevated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your right hand is exalted] or [your power is supreme]

Here, **arm** represents the power or control of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You have great power]

14.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **righteousness** and **justice**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [Acting rightly and judging fairly]

Ethan is using this possessive form to describe the base on which God’s rule rests. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the foundation on which your throne rests]
Here, **throne** represents God’s royal authority and rule. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your rule]

Ethan is speaking of **covenant faithfulness and truth** as if they were living things that could walk before God as attendants. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you always show covenant faithfulness and truth in everything you do]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **truth**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [being faithfully loving and being true to your promises]
Here, **face** represents God’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [go before you]

Here Ethan is speaking as if God’s rule were a building and righteousness and justice were its **foundation**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Your rule is based on righteousness and justice] or [You always rule righteously and justly]

15.note: Ethan is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of joy or blessing. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, how happy is] or [Truly blessed is]

Here Ethan is speaking as if people who live in God’s favor **walk in the light** of Yahweh’s face. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they live enjoying your favor] or [they live in the brightness of your presence]

Here Ethan is speaking as if living one’s life were **walking** along a path. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they live] or [they conduct their lives]

Ethan is using this possessive form to describe light that comes from God’s presence. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the light that shines from your face]
Here, **face** represents God’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your presence]

16.note: Ethan is using the term **name** to represent who the person is or to refer to the person’s reputation. Alternate translation: [Because of who you are]

Here Ethan is speaking as if being honored were to be physically rising **high**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and in your righteousness they are honored] or [and because you are righteous, you give them a high position]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [because you are righteous]

17.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **splendor**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the one who makes their strength splendid]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how strong they are]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **favor**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and because you desired the best for us]

Here Ethan is speaking as if power were a **horn** that could be raised up. In this case, it is likely that he means that Yahweh has allowed them to have a powerful king. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have allowed us to have a powerful king] or [you make us a strong nation]

18.note: Here Ethan is speaking of the king who protects them as if he were a battle **shield**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [our protector belongs to Yahweh] or [Yahweh is the one who gave us our protector]

Ethan is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and our king belongs to the Holy One of Israel]

Ethan is using this possessive form to describe the holy God with whom the Israelites are in a covenant relationship. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and our king belongs to the holy God with whom we Israelites are in a covenant relationship]

19.note: Ethan is using the word translated as **Then** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

19.q: וַ⁠תֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁוִּ֣יתִי עֵ֭זֶר עַל־גִּבּ֑וֹר הֲרִימ֖וֹתִי בָח֣וּר מֵ⁠עָֽם
19.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [telling them that you have placed help on a warrior; you have raised up a chosen one from the people]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **help**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my helping hand]

20.note: Ethan is using the possessive form to describe **oil** that is characterized by **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my holy oil]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with my holy oil]

21.note: The expression **my hand will be established** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [I will establish my hand]

Here, **hand** represents the power or dominion of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my power will be established]

Here, **arm** represents power or strength. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my power will also strengthen him]

22.note: God is using **son of** as a common expression of the culture to indicate that a person has a certain characteristic. In this case, the person has the characteristic of being wicked. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and a wicked person]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wickedness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [people acting wickedly]

23.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [I will completely destroy all of his enemies]

Here, **face** represents a person’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from before him] or [from his presence]

24.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **faithfulness** and **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [I will be faithful to him and loyally love him]

Here God is speaking as if David’s strength and honor were a **horn** lifted high. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and by my authority he will be exalted] or [and in my name he will be powerful]
God is using the term **name** to represent who the person is or to refer to the person’s reputation. Alternate translation: [by my authority]

25.note: Here, **hand** and **right hand** represent the power or dominion of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will give him dominion over the sea and authority over the rivers]

Here God is speaking as if David would physically place his hands on the sea and rivers to claim them. God means that David’s rule will extend across a vast territory. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And his rule will extend from the sea to the rivers] or [And he will rule over the land from the Mediterranean Sea to the Euphrates River]

26.q: ה֣וּא יִ֭קְרָאֵ⁠נִי אָ֣בִ⁠י אָ֑תָּה אֵ֝לִ֗⁠י וְ⁠צ֣וּר יְשׁוּעָתִֽ⁠י
26.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [He will call to me that I am his Father, his God, and the rock of his salvation]

God is stating the pronoun **He** separately, even though the verb already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that his chosen one is the one who will name God as his father. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [My chosen one will call to me]

Here God is speaking as if he were a **rock** that provides stability and protection. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the one who saves and protects me] or [my strong savior]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the rock who saves me]

27.note: God is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who will personally exalt David in response to David’s faithfulness. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [Indeed, I will make him]

Here God is speaking of David’s privileged status as if he were a **firstborn** son, who holds the most honored position in the family. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will give him the highest honor] or [I will give him the privileges of a firstborn son]

28.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I will always be loyally faithful to him]

29.note: Here God is speaking of David’s descendants as if they were **seed**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will establish his descendants forever]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the days of the heavens** endure without end, so will **his throne** endure. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and his throne will last as long as the heavens endure]

Here, **throne** represents royal authority and the right to rule. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and his royal authority]

30.note: Here, **If his sons forsake my law** introduces a possible condition. God will only do the things in the following verse if this condition happens. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen.

Here God is speaking as if people who obey his commands were **walking** along a path. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do not live according to my decrees] or [do not obey my rules]

30.q: אִם־יַֽעַזְב֣וּ בָ֭נָי⁠ו תּוֹרָתִ֑⁠י וּ֝⁠בְ⁠מִשְׁפָּטַ֗⁠י לֹ֣א יֵלֵכֽוּ⁠ן
30.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [If his sons completely reject and disobey my commandments]

30.q: אִם־יַֽעַזְב֣וּ בָ֭נָי⁠ו תּוֹרָתִ֑⁠י וּ֝⁠בְ⁠מִשְׁפָּטַ֗⁠י לֹ֣א יֵלֵכֽוּ⁠ן
30.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **law** and **judgments**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [If his sons forsake what I have taught them and do not walk in the way that I have told them to live]

31.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **statutes** and **commandments**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [if they profane the rules I have established and they do not do the things I have commanded them to do]

32.note: This verse introduces the consequence of the condition proposed in the previous verse. Use a natural form in your language for introducing the consequence of this possible condition. Alternate translation: [then I will visit]

Here, **rod** represents guiding, protecting, and directing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will discipline them for their transgression]

God is using this possessive forms, **their transgression** and **their iniquity**, to assign to them the ownership of their behaviors. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [then I will punish the transgression they commit with a rod and the iniquity they commit with blows]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **transgression** and **iniquity**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [then I will punish the ways they have rebelled with a rod and the wrong they have done with blows]

33.note: God uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the punishment he will bring in the previous verse and the loyal love he will not withdraw. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Nonetheless, my covenant faithfulness]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **faithfulness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [But I will not stop being loyally faithful to him, and I will not be unfaithful to what I promised]

34.note: Here, **the utterance of my lips** represents what God has spoken. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I will not change what I have spoken]

God is using the possessive form to describe what his **lips** have produced as speech. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and I will not change my words]

35.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by my holy character]

Following the custom of the culture, God is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (‘if’) but not the second part (‘then’). If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [I will certainly not lie to David!]

36.note: Here God is speaking of descendants as if they were **seed**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [His descendants will be forever]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the sun** is enduring and permanent, so is **his throne**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [his throne will endure permanently like the sun before me]

36.q: זַ֭רְע⁠וֹ לְ⁠עוֹלָ֣ם יִהְיֶ֑ה וְ⁠כִסְא֖⁠וֹ כַ⁠שֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ נֶגְדִּֽ⁠י
36.note: God is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [His seed will be forever, and his throne will be forever, like the sun before me]

37.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the moon** is permanent and enduring, so is **the dynasty of David**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [I will establish it forever, as permanent as the moon]

The expression **It will be established** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [I will establish it]
